subject: physics
question_text: A quantum processor has demonstrated quantum supremacy. What does this term mean?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 14 Very Short Answer Question 8 (printed p.143). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Chapter 14 is new to the 2026-27 syllabus and no board has examined it, so there is no exam history to cite. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: quantum supremacy (also called quantum advantage) is correctly defined as the point where a programmable quantum processor solves a problem no classical computer can solve in any practical amount of time; the book's named commercial processor is replaced with neutral wording per Rule 35.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: a problem a classical computer cannot
steps.why: Quantum supremacy is defined as the point where a programmable quantum processor solves a problem that no classical computer can finish in any practical amount of time.
common_mistakes: Saying the classical computer takes longer, instead of saying it cannot finish in a practical time.
Omitting the comparison with classical computers entirely.
steps.memory_tip: Definition: a quantum processor solves what no classical computer can finish in practical time.
steps.margin_note: Both names, quantum supremacy and quantum advantage, are accepted.

steps.label: The condition
lines: computers only on that one chosen task.
steps.why: This condition keeps quantum supremacy narrow: the quantum processor outperforms classical computers on the one task chosen for the demonstration, not on computing in general.
common_mistakes: Writing that quantum computers are now better than all computers in general.
Saying the quantum processor outperforms classical computers at every task, not just the one demonstrated.
steps.memory_tip: Condition: one task only, not general superiority over classical computers.
steps.margin_note: The words one task must appear. General superiority alone is not accepted.
